title: Mode reflection
blurb: Create 2D contexts on HTMLCanvasElement and OffscreenCanvas with every toneMapping value (omitted, {}, standard, extended, invalid), inspect getContextAttributes(), and run the 6-case WPT matrix.
question: Does getContext('2d', { toneMapping: { mode } }) validate CanvasToneMappingMode and reflect 'standard' and 'extended' identically on HTMLCanvasElement and OffscreenCanvas?
result: In Chrome 153 headless, flag-off scores 4/6 on the WPT matrix (extended reflects 'standard' and invalid modes do not throw); with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features invalid modes throw TypeError, while extended still reflects 'standard' (4/6). Full reflection requires Chrome 160+ or --enable-blink-features=CanvasToneMapping.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (flag off and --enable-experimental-web-platform-features); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Chrome 153 behind the experimental flag validates CanvasToneMappingMode but still reflects 'standard' when 'extended' is requested
friction.repro: Run canvas.getContext('2d', { toneMapping: { mode: 'extended' } }).getContextAttributes().toneMapping.mode with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features in Chrome 153; it returns 'standard' instead of 'extended'.
friction.workaround: Check getContextAttributes().toneMapping?.mode === 'extended' before assuming HDR output is active, and fall back to SDR rendering when it stays 'standard'.

friction.summary: toneMapping is fixed at first getContext('2d') creation and silently ignored on subsequent calls on the same canvas
friction.repro: Call getContext('2d', { toneMapping: { mode: 'standard' } }) then getContext('2d', { toneMapping: { mode: 'extended' } }) on the same canvas element; the original context and attributes are returned unchanged.
friction.workaround: Create a fresh canvas element or OffscreenCanvas when changing toneMapping mode, or use CSS dynamic-range-limit to adjust HDR headroom dynamically.
